edges.notes: glibc provides thin syscall wrappers and userland POSIX/C API atop the Linux kernel ABI.
GCC targets glibc on typical GNU/Linux triplets; shared bootstrap and ABI history.
GNU ld links against glibc shared objects; dynamic linker is part of the glibc package.
libc.so and ld-linux are ELF shared objects; PT_INTERP / dynamic linking story.
glibc is a major implementation of the C standard library portion of hosted C environments.
glibc includes ports for GNU/Linux targets including RISC-V alongside the psABI.
Clang-built binaries commonly link against glibc on GNU/Linux when using the gnu libc environment.
GDB debugs glibc-linked executables and shared libraries; libc debuginfo is common on distros.
LLDB on Linux often debugs processes linked against glibc similarly to GDB-centric flows.
Substitutable Linux libc implementations (glibc vs musl) with different ABI and feature sets.
Substitutable Unix libc implementations across Linux vs FreeBSD base system (not ABI-interchangeable).
Substitutable Unix libc implementations across Linux vs OpenBSD base system (not ABI-interchangeable).
Substitutable Unix libc implementations across Linux vs NetBSD base system (not ABI-interchangeable).
Substitutable Unix libc implementations across Linux vs DragonFly base system (not ABI-interchangeable).
Substitutable Unix libc implementations across Linux vs illumos distribution libc (not ABI-interchangeable).
Substitutable libc implementations across GNU/Linux glibc vs Android Bionic (not ABI-interchangeable).
Substitutable C library implementations across GNU/Linux glibc vs embedded newlib toolchains (not ABI-interchangeable).
Substitutable C library implementations across GNU/Linux glibc vs Wasm WASI wasi-libc (not ABI-interchangeable).
Substitutable Linux libc implementations across glibc vs uClibc (not ABI-interchangeable).
Substitutable Linux libc implementations across glibc vs dietlibc (not ABI-interchangeable).
GNU libstdc++ relies on glibc for many C/POSIX services underneath C++ standard library facilities on GNU/Linux.
libc++ on GNU/Linux sits on glibc for C/POSIX services under C++ standard library facilities.
libc++abi uses glibc-backed pthread and C services for hosted exception and runtime support on GNU/Linux.
Debian GNU/Linux uses glibc as the standard C library on mainstream architecture ports.
Ubuntu uses glibc as the standard C library on mainstream desktop and server ports.
Fedora uses glibc as the standard C library on mainstream architecture ports.
RHEL uses glibc as the standard C library on supported enterprise architecture ports.
Rocky Linux uses glibc as the standard C library on mainstream architecture ports.
AlmaLinux uses glibc as the standard C library on mainstream architecture ports.
CentOS Stream uses glibc as the standard C library on mainstream architecture ports.
Historical CentOS Linux releases used glibc as the standard C library on mainstream architecture ports.
